document.title: GitLab architecture overview
document.attribution: GitLab documentation, GitLab Inc. and contributors

individuals.title: GitLab
individuals.description: The GitLab application as a whole: the set of cooperating components and processes that together deliver GitLab.

evidence.quote: When deployed, GitLab should be considered the amalgamation of the below processes.
GitLab has several components to operate.

individuals.title: GitLab Rails
individuals.description: The core Ruby on Rails application: serves the web interface and the GitLab API, performs authorization checks and holds the application's configuration.

evidence.quote: used to run the core Rails Application that provides the user facing features in GitLab
GitLab is a Ruby on rails application

individuals.title: GitLab Workhorse
individuals.description: A smart reverse proxy written at GitLab that sits in front of Puma, handles large HTTP requests and serves static files directly.

evidence.quote: GitLab Workhorse is a program designed at GitLab to help alleviate pressure from Puma.
Smart reverse proxy, handles large HTTP requests

individuals.title: GitLab Shell
individuals.description: The add-on program that handles SSH-based git sessions and maintains the list of authorized keys.

evidence.quote: GitLab Shell is a program designed at GitLab to handle SSH-based `git` sessions, and modifies the list of authorized keys.
The add-on component GitLab Shell serves repositories over SSH.

individuals.title: Gitaly
individuals.description: The Git RPC service that handles all Git-level access in GitLab, executing Git operations for the other components.

evidence.quote: Gitaly is a service designed by GitLab to remove our need for NFS for Git storage in distributed deployments of GitLab
Git RPC service for handling all Git calls made by GitLab

individuals.title: Praefect
individuals.description: A transparent proxy between Git clients and Gitaly that coordinates replication of repository updates to secondary nodes.

evidence.quote:
Praefect is a transparent proxy between each Git client and the Gitaly coordinating the replication of
repository updates to secondary nodes.

individuals.title: GitLab Pages
individuals.description: The component that hosts static websites published directly from a repository.

evidence.quote: GitLab Pages is a feature that allows you to publish static websites directly from a repository in GitLab.
Hosts static websites

individuals.title: GitLab Runner
individuals.description: Runs GitLab CI/CD jobs and sends the results back to GitLab.

evidence.quote: GitLab Runner runs jobs and sends the results to GitLab.
Executes GitLab CI/CD jobs

individuals.title: GitLab agent for Kubernetes
individuals.description: An in-cluster component that integrates GitLab with Kubernetes, for example to sync deployments onto a cluster.

evidence.quote:
The GitLab agent for Kubernetes is an active in-cluster
component for solving GitLab and Kubernetes integration tasks in a secure and
cloud-native way.

individuals.title: GitLab agent server
individuals.description: The server side of the Kubernetes agent, reached through NGINX on TCP 8150 (appears in the component diagram only).

evidence.quote: GitLabKas[GitLab agent server] --> GitLabWorkhorse

individuals.title: GitLab Exporter
individuals.description: An in-house process that exports metrics about GitLab application internals to Prometheus.

evidence.quote: GitLab Exporter is a process designed in house that allows us to export metrics about GitLab application internals to Prometheus.

individuals.title: AI Gateway
individuals.description: A standalone service that gives every GitLab instance, self-managed or SaaS, access to AI features.

evidence.quote:
GitLab AI Gateway is a standalone-service that will give access to AI features to all users of
GitLab
A SaaS model gateway is available to enable AI-native features.

individuals.title: GitLab Duo Workflow Service
individuals.description: The service behind GitLab's agentic AI features, deployed through Runway.

evidence.quote: GitLab Duo Workflow Service is our agentic AI Features that is deployed via our Runway service

individuals.title: Registry
individuals.description: The container registry where users store their own Docker images; it delegates authentication to GitLab.

evidence.quote: The registry is what users use to store their own Docker images.
Container registry, allows pushing and pulling of images

individuals.title: Token Revocation API
individuals.description: A GitLab.com-only component that receives and revokes leaked secrets.

evidence.quote: Receives and revokes leaked secrets

individuals.description: An executable provided by GitLab Shell that the SSH server calls to look up the presented key through the Rails internal API.

evidence.quote:
`AuthorizedKeysCommand` is an executable provided by

individuals.description: The executable that replaces AuthorizedKeysCommand when SSH certificates are used; it extracts a username from the certificate.

evidence.quote:
`AuthorizedKeysCommand` is replaced with an
`AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand`

individuals.title: AuthorizedKeysWorker
individuals.description: A background worker in Rails that keeps the authorized_keys file up to date whenever a user changes an SSH key.

evidence.quote:
This is kept up to date by an `AuthorizedKeysWorker`
in Rails, scheduled to run whenever an SSH key is modified by a user.

individuals.title: Git over HTTP request
individuals.description: How a Git fetch or push over HTTP is handled jointly by Workhorse, Rails and Gitaly using the stateless smart protocol.

evidence.quote:
Git operations over HTTP use the stateless "smart" protocol described in the
